name: CA-15
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Kevin Mullin running with a large fundraising edge
Republican challenger Charles Hoelter has no reported fundraising
model.rationale: The district's +26 Democratic lean, Mullin's incumbency and roughly $820,000 raised against an unfunded challenger, and prediction markets pricing a Democratic win near 96% all point to a safe Democratic hold. No polls or expert ratings exist, so uncertainty stays moderately wide despite the lopsided fundamentals.
model.watch: A surprise surge of Republican outside spending or unusually low Democratic turnout in a low-profile California general could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Kevin Mullin, the Democratic incumbent, advanced to the general election against Republican Charles Hoelter in a Bay Area district that leans Democratic by about 26 points. Mullin has raised roughly $820,000 and holds about $220,000 on hand, while Hoelter shows no reported fundraising and no outside spending on either side. Prediction markets put the Democratic chance of winning near 96 percent.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the forecast rests on the district's partisan lean, incumbency, and the large financial gap. All of these favor Mullin heavily, making this a safe Democratic seat with only modest residual uncertainty about the final margin.
